newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Poison biscuit extortion threat in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Poison biscuit extortion threat in Australia.

text.p: An extortionist has threatened to plant poisoned biscuits in supermarkets unless police undergo a lie detector test over an old murder case, Australian police said on Thursday.

Queensland police superintendent Ron Pickering told a news conference that an extortion letter and packages containing poisoned biscuits were received by a leading food company in the states of New South Wales and Queensland on February 3.
Pickering would not reveal the company name, but the domestic news agency Australian Associated Press reported that the company was Arnotts.

The extortionist demanded that New South Wales police involved in a murder investigation several years ago undergo "public polygraph tests" by February 17 or a popular brand of biscuits would be laced with poison and planted on supermarket shelves in both states.
The letter said New South Wales police had set up a man for the murder of a bookmaker in 1991.
Police were forced to make public the extortion threat on Thursday after a media organisation broke an embargo on the threat.
"We believed from the outset that there was no threat to public safety until February 17," Pickering said.
"We had appealed to media to keep an embargo while police investigations were carried out."
